players.product: ALD & epitaxy systems (GAA, backside power delivery)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Paul Verhagen: Q2 2026 revenue was EUR 1 billion, above the EUR 980 million guidance and the first quarter above EUR 1 billion (CEO), up 24% year on year and 15% on Q1 at constant currency; equipment sales rose 22% at constant currency on record ALD sales, and Spares & Services grew 34% on outcome-based services and elevated customer fab utilization. Gross margin was 51.9%, SG&A 7.9% of revenue, net R&D up 22% (11.1% of revenue), and adjusted operating profit rose 27% at a 33% margin, in line with Q1's record. Free cash flow was a record EUR 355 million and cash EUR 1.2 billion; ASM's share of income from its approximately 24.6% stake in ASMPT was EUR 9 million.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 2026 revenue EUR 1 billion, +24% year on year at constant currency

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Paul Verhagen: in H1 2026 Logic Foundry accounted for 77% of equipment sales, memory 15% (16% in full-year 2025, on shipment phasing) and power / analog / wafer 8%. In leading-edge Logic Foundry, 2nm-related sales were the largest part while 3nm-7nm sales showed a nice uptick; mature Logic Foundry stayed solid with China the majority. CEO Hichem M'Saad: growing demand for advanced CPUs and agentic AI workloads is tightening capacity and driving demand for the ALD-intensive 3nm-7nm nodes after limited spending in the past couple of years.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 2026 equipment sales: Logic Foundry 77%, memory 15%

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Hichem M'Saad: ASM expects Q3 revenue of EUR 1.1 billion and H2 revenue up over 20% versus H1 at constant currency, led by advanced Logic Foundry (2nm, 3nm-7nm and a first meaningful 1.4nm contribution) and a substantial memory increase; 2026 revenue will exceed EUR 4 billion, and 2027 revenue is now expected to exceed the top end of the EUR 3.7 billion-EUR 4.6 billion range shared at the September 2025 Investor Day. CEO: if WFE grows 30%, ASM will grow at least at that level. CFO Paul Verhagen: full-year gross margin around 51% and SG&A below 8.5% of sales. CEO: the only segment expected to be down in H2 is mature Logic Foundry, reflecting the first-half-weighted nature of its sales this year.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 2026 revenue EUR 1.1 billion; 2026 revenue above EUR 4 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Hichem M'Saad: memory sales rose in Q2 mainly on HBM-related DRAM, Q2 memory orders were a record quarterly high, and H2 memory sales should rise substantially, driven primarily by advanced HBM DRAM and to a lesser extent by China. ASM was selected by another DRAM customer for its epitaxy solution; CFO Paul Verhagen: the new win brings maybe one or two tools this year and meaningful revenue in 2027. CEO: the DRAM transition to 4F squared cells and FinFET-based peripheral circuitry, expected in production in the 2028-2030 timeframe, will raise ASM's DRAM served available market by EUR 400 million-EUR 450 million over the next two nodes; ASM is already in high-volume manufacturing in EPI with one memory customer, and some customers' hiccups moving to 4F squared are not consequential because ALD and epitaxy are already penetrating at 6F squared.
quarterly_data.figure: DRAM SAM +EUR 400 million-EUR 450 million over the next two nodes

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Hichem M'Saad: orders for the 1.4nm node are happening now; ASM ships 1.4nm tools in the second half of 2026 as customers invest in pilot lines and will ship even more in 2027, ahead of 1.4nm high-volume manufacturing in 2028. Some customers view 1.4nm as a potentially larger opportunity than 2nm, ASM's served market there grows, and it expects its 1.4nm share to strengthen versus 2nm in both ALD and EPI. ASM won new molybdenum ALD applications at 1.4nm in the past quarter, its first use in the metal deposition market; the CEO calls moly 'not a very huge market' that will proliferate gradually from one generation to the next. CFO Paul Verhagen: ASM already knew last quarter which customers it would ship 1.4nm to.

CFO Paul Verhagen: the order book typically covers six to nine months and is perhaps a little better than normal; customer commitments, though not yet formal orders, are firmer than in prior years, H1 orders were very strong and strong H2 orders are expected. CEO Hichem M'Saad: customers are giving equipment plans for 2027 and some even for 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: order book six to nine months

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Paul Verhagen: stress across the shared semiconductor supply base is increasing as the whole industry ramps; ASM works with suppliers to secure its allocation, develops dual and triple sourcing and places people at stressed suppliers, and the situation is 'so far manageable'. ASM is implementing targeted price increases where possible to pass on supplier cost inflation while keeping value-based pricing. CEO Hichem M'Saad: having invested ahead of the curve in its Singapore and Korea manufacturing sites, ASM is well positioned to increase output.

CFO Paul Verhagen: China demand is very strong, partly because speculation about new export controls brings some accelerated ordering, 'not excessive'; overall China sales should stay solid in H2, with memory and power / wafer / analog growth largely offsetting lower mature Logic Foundry, and in 2027 the bulk of China should again be mature Logic Foundry, with visibility low. CEO Hichem M'Saad: ASM does not ship tools for leading-edge devices in China and stays competitive against many local players by lowering cost of ownership; power / wafer / analog is recovering, linked to AI data-center power needs, with good recent activity in silicon carbide epitaxy.

CFO Paul Verhagen: Q2 capex was EUR 63 million and full-year capex is expected above the top of the EUR 150 million-EUR 250 million range, mostly for the construction of the new Scottsdale site; working capital improved to 50 days from 69. The CMP acquisition complements ASM's deposition business and supports its goal to grow in advanced packaging. CEO Hichem M'Saad: advanced packaging is an attractive medium-term growth opportunity as chiplets and heterogeneous integration raise the importance of materials, bonding and interface engineering, and the PECVD patterning solution is gaining encouraging customer engagement for its gap-fill capability.
